_comment: The TTCircle underwriting model. These are the same factors the Apps Script backend applies, kept here so the quotation page can show the student a live estimate before submitting. Keep both in step: if you change a factor here, change it in Code.gs too.
_insuredValueNote: Trade practice: cargo is insured at CIF value plus 10% for the buyer's expected profit and incidental costs. The premium is rated on the insured value, not on the invoice value.

CIF.note: Incoterms 2020, CIF A5: the seller must obtain cargo insurance complying with Institute Cargo Clauses (C) as a minimum. Wider cover may be agreed between the parties.

CIP.note: Incoterms 2020, CIP A5: the seller must obtain cargo insurance complying with Institute Cargo Clauses (A), all risks.

iccDescriptions.ICC(A): All risks — the broadest cover, protecting against physical loss or damage from any external cause except the listed exclusions.
iccDescriptions.ICC(B): Named perils — covers the ICC(C) list plus earthquake, lightning, washing overboard and water entering the vessel or container.
iccDescriptions.ICC(C): Basic — major casualties only: fire, explosion, sinking, stranding, overturning, collision and general average.

incotermDescriptions.EXW: Ex Works — the buyer bears all risk from the seller's premises.
incotermDescriptions.FCA: Free Carrier — risk transfers when the goods are handed to the carrier.
incotermDescriptions.FAS: Free Alongside Ship — risk transfers alongside the vessel.
incotermDescriptions.FOB: Free On Board — risk transfers once the goods are on board.
incotermDescriptions.CPT: Carriage Paid To — the seller pays the freight, the buyer bears the risk.
incotermDescriptions.CIP: Carriage and Insurance Paid To — the seller insures at ICC(A).
incotermDescriptions.CFR: Cost and Freight — the seller pays the freight but does not insure.
incotermDescriptions.CIF: Cost, Insurance and Freight — the seller insures at ICC(B) minimum.
incotermDescriptions.DAP: Delivered At Place — the seller bears the risk until delivery.
incotermDescriptions.DPU: Delivered at Place Unloaded — risk transfers after unloading.
incotermDescriptions.DDP: Delivered Duty Paid — the seller bears the maximum responsibility.

_referencesNote: Where the model comes from. Shown at the foot of the quotation page so a student can go and read the source instead of trusting the simulator.

items.title: Institute Cargo Clauses (A), 1/1/09
items.note: All risks, subject to the listed exclusions. Reaches theft and water damage.

items.title: Institute Cargo Clauses (B), 1/1/09
items.note: Named perils. Reaches water damage, not theft.

items.title: Institute Cargo Clauses (C), 1/1/09
items.note: Major casualties only. Neither theft nor water damage.

items.title: Institute Frozen/Chilled Food Clauses (A)
items.note: In the market this replaces ICC for chilled cargo such as fruit. The simulator keeps ICC and adds an extension instead, to hold the exercise on one scale.

items.title: Institute Frozen/Chilled Food Clauses (A) — 24 Hours Breakdown
items.note: The source of our reefer breakdown extension. Requires the machinery to be out for not less than 24 consecutive hours.

items.title: Institute Frozen/Chilled Meat Extension Clauses
items.note: The meat equivalent. It does not apply to fruit.

items.title: ICC Publication 723
items.note: CIF A5 obliges the seller to cover ICC(C) as a minimum; CIP A5 obliges ICC(A). These are the only cover minimums that bind.

items.title: Convention on the Contract for the International Carriage of Goods by Road, 1956
items.note: Art. 30.1, seven days to give notice of non-apparent damage; art. 30.3, twenty-one days for delay. Limit 8.33 SDR per kilogram.

items.title: Hague Rules as amended by the Visby Protocol
items.note: Art. III r. 6, three days. Limit 2 SDR per kilogram or 666.67 SDR per package, whichever is higher.

items.title: Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules for International Carriage by Air
items.note: Art. 31.2, fourteen days. Limit 22 SDR per kilogram.

references.caveat: TTCircle is a training simulator. Its rates, factors and thresholds are invented for teaching and are not a market tariff. The clauses, conventions and trade terms above are real, and where the simulator departs from them it says so.

additionalCoverages.label: ISRCC — Strikes, riots and civil commotion
IWC — Institute War Clauses
additionalCoverages.note: Institute War Clauses (Cargo), CL385. In the market the waters that attract a war rate are set by the Joint War Committee listed areas, not by the country.

additionalCoverages.label: Extraordinary risks (natural disaster, seizure, nuclear)
additionalCoverages.note: A TTCircle teaching bundle. It has no single counterpart in the Institute clauses.

additionalCoverages.label: Reefer breakdown — failure of the refrigerating machinery
additionalCoverages.note: Simplified from Institute Frozen/Chilled Food Clauses (A) — 24 Hours Breakdown, CL423. The real clause responds only where the machinery has been out for not less than 24 consecutive hours; ours pays on any failure. Note also that chilled cargo is normally written on CL430 in place of ICC, not on ICC plus an extension — the extension here keeps the exercise on one scale. CL422 is the food extension set; CL429 is the equivalent for meat and does not apply to fruit.

additionalCoverages.label: TPND — theft, pilferage and non-delivery. Already inside ICC(A); buy it over ICC(B) or ICC(C).
additionalCoverages.note: A market extension, not an Institute clause with its own number. ICC(A) (CL382) already reaches theft as an all-risks peril; ICC(B) (CL383) and ICC(C) (CL384) do not.
